object_description: sequence of three joined irregular hexagonal houses of different heights
design_condition: the building mass is organised as a sequence of hexagonal houses whose height development leads from the scale of the existing buildings in the east to that of the neighbouring courtyard building

positive: The height development of the houses leads convincingly from the scale of the existing eastern buildings to that of the neighbouring courtyard building
The indentations open up spaces around the two trees worth preserving in a very natural way
The corner towards the village centre offers a different outdoor quality with a forecourt, cafe terrace and a few trees
The scale of the hexagon containing the hall is well in keeping with the neighbouring courtyard building
The well-proportioned courtyard entrances guide visitors and adequately protect the surrounding housing from emissions
The hall and its adjoining rooms are functionally organised correctly, with an attractive entrance, foyer and hall sequence
The irregularly hexagonal hall is pleasantly proportioned and spanned by a ceiling of triangular panels
The storage and extension room has a high utility value
The polygonal volumes speak an unconventional architectural language referring to the local anthroposophical formal language
The apartments on the upper floors are efficiently organised and have recessed loggias
The project makes full use of the permitted use, giving a high utilisation rate and good economic efficiency
negative: As a public building the single-storey hall could have a little more charisma
The indentations do not quite correspond to the typical green spaces, as they offer no views into the spaces behind
Upgrading the inner courtyard to a neighbourhood square contradicts the concessions of its owners, and the courtyard lacks the location and potential
The proposed delivery via the streetcar crossing is not tolerated by the operator
The load-bearing effect of the statically effective wooden ribs is unclear
The stage does not meet the requirements of the programme and reads as a peep box attached to the hall rather than part of it
The strong beam above the stage emphasises the separation of stage and hall
The apartments above the stage are considered problematic for acoustic reasons
Some apartments have an almost exclusively northern orientation towards the streetcar, harming market absorption
The view from the west-facing apartments over the rising sheet metal roofs is unsatisfactory
The coherent form allows no views through, so an element typical of the district is lost
The close interlocking of hall use with residential use causes more disadvantages than advantages and makes finding a developer difficult
